questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to get a pay rise in a staff job
Unusual job titles from the 19th century
The good and bad sides of working for yourself
Why the pandemic closed many businesses
questions.why: They talk about working freelance and the advantages and disadvantages of it.

questions.q: Why does Rob like his current job?
options: It's creative, varied and secure
He can work from home every day of the week
He is his own boss
It pays much more than other jobs
questions.why: Rob says it's creative with lots of variety, and it's permanent with regular income and a pension.

questions.q: According to Rob, why do businesses need workers to work in different ways now?
options: Because workers want more holidays and shorter working days
Because the law about working hours has recently changed
Because there are fewer people looking for jobs these days
Because business needs change often, so firms must be flexible
questions.why: Rob says business needs change frequently and companies need to be agile.

questions.q: How did Carla Barker feel about leaving her permanent job?
options: Relaxed and confident
Very frightened and full of doubts
Angry with her old boss
Bored with her old routine
questions.why: She calls it 'a bit petrifying' and 'super-scary', and wondered if she was good enough.

questions.q: Which of these was NOT a reason Fiona Thomas gave for leaving her 9 to 5 job?
options: Wanting creative fulfilment
Needing flexibility for her mental health
Wanting to travel around the world
Wanting financial freedom
questions.why: She mentions creative fulfilment, flexibility for her mental health and financial freedom, but not travel.

questions.q: What kind of job did Fiona Thomas have before?
options: A face-to-face job in hospitality
A job as a writer
A job in a bank
A job delivering newspapers
questions.why: She says her job was very customer based, working face-to-face in hospitality.

questions.q: Why did her old job make Fiona's depression and anxiety worse?
options: The pay was too low for the hours
Fixed hours and crowds of people
Her colleagues were unkind
She had to travel a long way to work
questions.why: She says a rigid schedule and being in front of many people really exacerbated her symptoms.

questions.q: What risk does Rob point out about financial freedom?
options: You have to pay more taxes to the government
Your boss controls your money
You can never earn more
Nobody else controls your income
questions.why: Rob says the money isn't controlled by someone else, but 'that can be risky too'.
